stops.name: Buenos Aires, the record with no first page
stops.date_confidence: placeholder: no birth date, birthplace, cohort year, prior school, or graduation year is recorded in any reachable source, including her own university's graduate profile; the date shown marks the earliest work she herself documents, not a beginning
stops.campa: Every source that names her begins in the middle. The university that granted her degree publishes a profile with her contact address, her method, her credits and her pseudonym, and gives no year of birth, no city, no school before it. Her own portfolio opens on work already made. The earliest date she puts in writing is 2019, and behind that the paper stops. She enters the record as a dancer already trained and already composing. Where she trained, and with whom, and for how long, is set down by nobody, herself included.

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, the licenciatura in choreographic composition
stops.date_confidence: year unrecorded; UNA's graduate directory lists the degree with no cohort and no date, and the placement here is arbitrary within her documented span
stops.campa: The Departamento de Artes del Movimiento keeps its house at Martín Rodríguez 444 in La Boca, inside the Distrito de las Artes, a few blocks up from the Riachuelo. Here the Universidad Nacional de las Artes grants her the Licenciatura en Composición Coreográfica, mención Danza. The directory that lists its graduates gives four words before it gives anything else: creadora, bailarina, directora escénica y docente. Then the degree, spelled out in full. The page gives no entry year and no year of completion, names no thesis, and goes on from there to her email address.
stops.quote: Creadora, bailarina, directora escénica y docente. Licenciada en Composición Coreográfica mención Danza.
stops.quote_source: UNA, Área Transdepartamental de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile page, fetched 2026-08-16

stops.name: La Boca, the archive crossed with the popular languages
stops.date_confidence: undated: the profile page carries no publication date; the sentence is her standing description of her practice as the university prints it
stops.campa: The same page states what she does with the training, in a single sentence. She works to denaturalize the habits of composition and creation in academic scenic dance, by the historical reconstruction of a local archive and its crossing with popular languages. Which archive, the page does not say. The popular languages are easier to point at, and the page points at them further down: the pole competitions and the nightclub floors, entered under a second name. Whether the archive is one she assembled herself or one she found already made, no reachable source answers.
stops.quote: Su trabajo artístico consiste en desnaturalizar los hábitos de composición y creación en danza académica escénica a través de la reconstrucción histórica de un archivo local y el cruce con lenguajes populares.
suggested_refs: The unnamed 'archivo local' of her stated method, identified in no reachable source
sources: UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile, https://movimiento.una.edu.ar/graduadxs/massacesi-emilia_26

stops.name: El Taller de Omar, Solos Compartidos begun with Lucila Schmidt
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; the portfolio gives 2019 to 2021 for the run and no months
stops.campa: El Taller de Omar is a room in Buenos Aires that no map service holds: no entry and no street number in anything reachable. Two of her works live there. The first is Solos Compartidos, a bill of two solos titled Café Mandolina and Pigmenta, co-directed and danced with Lucila Schmidt, running from 2019 through 2021. Three years of one bill in one room. It is the earliest work her own portfolio records, and the credit she takes on it is co-directora e intérprete.

stops.name: El Taller de Omar, Un rocío llamado Automovilina
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no month or run length is given
stops.campa: In the same room, in 2021, she directs and dances Un rocío llamado Automovilina. The credit line in her portfolio reads directora e intérprete, with no co-author this time. The title puts dew and gasoline into one phrase. Of what happens on the floor the document keeps nothing, and no programme, press notice or recording of the piece has been located. What survives of it is a photograph on page seven of a portfolio she assembled herself, a year, and the name of a room that advertises itself nowhere.

stops.name: Centro Cultural Haroldo Conti, Yéssica de Adrogué
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the portfolio gives no month
stops.campa: At the Centro Cultural Haroldo Conti, on the Avenida del Libertador in the grounds of the former ESMA, she dances in Yéssica de Adrogué, directed by Rodrigo Arena. She is intérprete here, not author. The encounter opens the longest working relationship in her record: Arena will direct her at the international festival in 2022, at a rock club in Abasto the same year, and will still be putting her on a stage in a Barracas warehouse five years later. Almost every stage credit she holds outside her own two works passes through him.

stops.name: Paseo La Plaza, the New Face medal and the second name
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the portfolio dates the competition to 2021 and gives no month
stops.campa: Paseo La Plaza on Corrientes, a theatre complex built into an old market, hosts Exotic Generation Argentina. She enters the New Face category under the name Emilia Portman and takes the silver medal with a routine called Medusa, photographed by Natah Szuka. It is the first competition in her file and the first appearance of the second name. Years later the university will print that pseudonym in its own graduate directory, in the paragraph directly beneath the licenciatura.

stops.name: Teatro Libre, Bogotá, the choreography prize
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the portfolio gives 2022 and no month
stops.campa: Exotic Generation goes continental and she flies to Bogotá, to the Teatro Libre in Chapinero, with a routine titled Kitsune Kitten Fantasy. She comes back carrying two things: the silver medal in the Flow category, and the prize for Mejor Coreografía. The second belongs to both of her names at once. A licenciada en composición coreográfica has been judged the best choreographer at a Latin American exotic pole competition. No results page from the event was reachable; the whole of the record for the prize is page eleven of her portfolio, where the photograph is credited to Pole Maniax.

stops.name: Teatro del Globo, the bronze in heels
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no month recorded
stops.campa: The Pole-up tournament, at the Teatro del Globo on Marcelo T. de Alvear, High Heels Pro category. Her routine is a free adaptation of the anime Naruto, and she dances it in heels, as the category requires. She takes the bronze. It is her third medal in two years and her third category, after New Face and Flow, each of the three judged under a different rulebook. Page twelve of her portfolio holds a line of type about it and one photograph, credited to Romina Soledad.

stops.name: Edificio La Prensa, contemporary dance on trial
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; FIBA 2022 dates not recorded in the portfolio
stops.campa: Avenida de Mayo 575, the old Edificio de La Prensa, built for a newspaper and kept now as the city's house of culture, hosts the Festival Internacional de Buenos Aires. She performs in El caso Arena Rodrigo contra la danza contemporánea, directed by Rodrigo Arena, a piece whose title puts its own director in the dock against the form he works in. Her credit is intérprete. Her university's profile records a festival appearance for 2022 and names no venue; the venue comes from page five of her portfolio, where the photograph is credited to Evelyn Caneto.

stops.name: El Cultural San Martín, a season rather than a slot
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the portfolio records the season with no dates and no performance count
stops.campa: Sarmiento 1551, the house that has called itself El Cultural San Martín since its relaunch in 2016 and was the Centro Cultural General San Martín before that. El caso Arena plays a season here in the same year it plays the festival. A season is weeks of a run rather than a single billed night, and the difference is the difference between a tour date and a home. How many nights it ran, and to what house, her portfolio does not say. It records the whole of the season in six words: Temporada El Cultural San Martín, CABA, 2022.

stops.name: Teatro Auditorium, Mar del Plata, the piece leaves the capital
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; festival dates not recorded
stops.campa: At the Teatro Auditorium on the seafront in Mar del Plata, four hundred kilometres down the coast, the production plays the Festival Cuerpx, Arte y Género. This festival sorts work by its subject and not by its form, so a trial of contemporary dance is programmed here as a question about bodies and gender. The title does not change and the cast does not change; the argument printed around it does. It is the first time her name travels outside Buenos Aires on a poster, and her portfolio marks the whole appearance with a city, a festival and a year.

stops.name: Teatro Lavardén, Rosario, the third city
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no dates given for the festival appearance
stops.campa: Mendoza and Sarmiento in Rosario, the Teatro Lavardén, an early twentieth-century house standing three hundred kilometres up the Paraná from the capital, takes the piece for the Festival El Cruce. It is the third city of the year for the same production. Mar del Plata, then Rosario, then Bahía Blanca: this tour is the whole of her documented travel inside Argentina, and no other work of hers is recorded leaving Buenos Aires. Her portfolio gives the house, the festival and the year in a single line, on the same page as the other four.

sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.5
Coordinates: Teatro Lavardén (Plataforma Lavardén), Mendoza 1085, Rosario; approximate

stops.name: Teatro Municipal de Bahía Blanca, the tour's last stop
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the festival edition's dates are not recorded in the portfolio
stops.campa: The Teatro Municipal of Bahía Blanca, on Alsina, takes it for the Festival Internacional de Artes Escénicas Bahía Teatro, six hundred kilometres southwest of Buenos Aires. The piece is two seasons old and still being programmed. Her portfolio lists all five venues of the production in a single block of text, with a year attached to each and nothing else attached to any of them: no cast list, no running time, no review, and no way of telling whether she danced all five houses or joined the tour partway. There is no photograph from this city on any page of it.

sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.5

stops.name: Buenos Aires, teaching Danza Moderna and the Método Muller
stops.date_confidence: undated: the profile states the teaching without years or a list of schools; the date is a placement within her documented span
stops.campa: She teaches Danza Moderna and the Método Muller in schools and studios across the city and Greater Buenos Aires. The method carries a name and behind the name a line. Jennifer Muller joined José Limón's company at eighteen, stayed with it into the 1970s, founded her own in 1974, and set work as far south as this city. Behind Limón stand the American teachers of expressive movement, Genevieve Stebbins reading François Delsarte, a nineteenth-century French grammar of gesture that reached Buenos Aires by way of New York. In the studios of the Gran Buenos Aires it is taught as technique, under the name of the woman nearest the end of that line.
stops.quote: Se desempeña como docente de Danza Moderna y Método Muller en diversas escuelas y estudios de la Ciudad y del Gran Buenos Aires.
suggested_refs: Jennifer Muller / MULLERWORKS technique, and its transmission into Buenos Aires studios
sources: UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile
